description: Answers the questions homeowners ask before they call: cost, timing, licensing and insurance, warranties, financing, emergencies and service area. It handles objections, adds long-tail SEO copy and should always end with a way to reach a human.
queries: FAQ section next to a photo with contact call to action

references.layout: A giant 2-line heading spans the full width, centered, with small red '+' marks at the far left and right margins. A centered 2-line sub follows. Below, full-width category rows (~30px tall, hairlines) each show a '+' or '×' at the far left, the category name at ~8% in, a grey description at ~58% and a grey 'N essential questions' count flush right. The open category reveals a nested accordion in the right half, with questions, '+' icons and an answer paragraph.
references.type: Heading in a neo-grotesk at ~72px medium, all caps, line-height ~0.9, tight tracking. Sub ~14px medium. Category names ~10px. Descriptions and counts ~8px grey. Nested questions ~10px semibold.
references.color: White ground, black ~#111111 type, grey ~#8A8A8A meta, hairlines ~#E2E2E2, signal red ~#FF3B12 for the corner '+' marks.
details: Question counts per category ('5 essential questions') set expectations and invite a click
Two-level accordion: categories first, then questions, so a long FAQ stays short on screen
Each category gets a one-line description ('Costs, availability, and how to get started')
Red registration '+' marks at the edges echo the brand's technical system
references.why_it_works: It scales to 25+ questions without becoming a wall, and the huge heading makes FAQ a confident chapter rather than an afterthought.
references.trade_adaptation: Plumber: categories 'Emergencies' (what counts, response time), 'Pricing' (flat rate, trip fee), 'Warranty', 'Water heaters', 'Service area', each with a count and a one-line description.

references.layout: A 2-line heading top-left, and a diagonal-split box holding the section number '06' top-right. Accordion rows (~80% width, offset right) are white boxes with 1px outlines. Each has a tiny numbered tab ('01') notched into the top-left corner, the question, and a separate right-hand cell with an ↑ or ↓ arrow. The open row shows two long answer paragraphs with bold phrases. A small promo card with a book cover and an orange button sits bottom-right.
references.type: Heading in a heavy condensed grotesk at ~56px, all caps. Questions ~16px regular. Answers ~10px with bold emphasis. Number tabs ~7px.
references.color: Light grey ~#D4D4D4 ground with ~#C2C2C2 grid lines, electric blue ~#2A1AFF type and outlines, white fills, orange ~#FF5A1F promo button.
details: Numbered tabs notched into the box corners look like file-folder tabs
The arrow sits in its own outlined column, which turns the toggle into a deliberate control
Grid-paper ground and a single ink color give a blueprint or work-order aesthetic
A lead magnet sits beside the FAQ ('MARKETING FREEBIE')
references.why_it_works: Distinctive with only two colors. It feels engineered and confident, which suits contractors who want to look sharp and modern.
references.trade_adaptation: Bold electrician or garage-door brand: '01 Do you charge for estimates?', '02 Are you licensed & insured?', '03 How fast can you come out?', with a side card offering a 'Free home safety checklist (PDF)'.

references.layout: A sticky left column (~38%) holds a 2-line heading, a 4-line friendly paragraph and a pill 'Contact us' button. The right column (~45%) is grouped by colored subheads ('Getting Started', 'Services & Sessions'). Under each, questions sit on hairline dividers with a '+' inside a small tinted circle at the right. A thick colored frame borders the whole page.
references.type: Heading in a neo-grotesk at ~22px bold. Paragraph ~11px. Group subheads ~14px medium in blue. Questions ~10px regular.
references.color: White panel inside a lime ~#A6EE8A frame, black text, royal blue ~#1F5BFF subheads and button, blue-grey ~#9DB0CF dividers, pink ~#F9C9D2 icon circles with blue '+'.
details: Grouped subheads in color break a long list into scannable chapters
Soft pink circles behind the '+' icons make the toggles feel friendly
The contact CTA stays visible on the left while you read
The intro paragraph speaks to the reader ('don't hesitate to reach out, we're always happy to help')
references.why_it_works: Warm, organized and accessible. The split keeps help one tap away, which is the real job of an FAQ.
references.trade_adaptation: House cleaner or pest control: groups 'Before your first visit', 'Pricing & payment', 'Safety (kids & pets)', with 'Do you bring your own supplies?' and 'Is treatment pet-safe?'. A 'Text us' button stays fixed on the left.

references.layout: Left (~40%): a small lead line, a condensed heading, a 4-line paragraph and a khaki button. Right (~48%): the open question with a '×' at the right, then a rich answer (an intro sentence, a bulleted list with bold lead-ins, a closing sentence), then the next question with a '+'. Hairlines throughout.
references.type: Heading 'FAQS' in a condensed bold grotesk at ~32px, all caps. Questions ~13px medium. Answer body ~10px, with bold lead-ins ('Workplace Strategy:') in each bullet.
references.color: White ground, black ~#111111 text, hairlines ~#DADADA, stone ~#C9C4B0 button.
details: Answers are structured content (bullets with bold lead-ins), not a single paragraph
The closing sentence of the answer restates the benefit
The button points to a fuller FAQ page ('To our FAQ'), so the home-page version stays short
references.why_it_works: It treats answers as real sales copy and gives rich detail without clutter. The condensed heading keeps the brand's industrial voice.
references.trade_adaptation: Roofer: 'How do you handle storm damage?' answered with bullets: 'Emergency tarping: same day…', 'Insurance claims: we meet your adjuster…', 'Repair or replace: honest assessment…'.

references.layout: Three zones: a 'F.A.Q' heading with a 2-line sub on the left (~25%), numbered question rows in the center (~42%), and a 'Still have questions? Our team is here to help.' note with a mono 'EMAIL US' link and a circular outline button on the right. A black CTA band with faint concentric arcs follows directly.
references.type: 'F.A.Q' in a squared, wide display grotesk (Eurostile or Michroma style) at ~36px bold with periods. Row numbers ~7px grey. Questions ~10px. CTA band headline in the same squared display at ~36px, all caps.
references.color: White ground, black text, grey ~#9A9A9A numbers, hairlines ~#E6E6E6. Black ~#141414 CTA band with faint ~#2A2A2A arcs and white type.
details: The squared, wide display face reads as transport or industrial signage
The 'still have questions' escape hatch sits in the same row as the FAQ, not below it
The FAQ hands straight off to a bold CTA band ('READY TO MOVE SMARTER?')
Small numbered rows ('07', '08') feel like an index
references.why_it_works: Industrial character from one typeface choice, and the three-zone layout pairs answers with a contact route.
references.trade_adaptation: Garage-door or moving-adjacent trade: 'Can you service commercial roll-up doors?', 'Do you carry parts on the truck?', with 'Still stuck? Call (555) 018-4400' on the right, then a black 'READY FOR A DOOR THAT WORKS?' band.

references.layout: A 2-line serif heading top-left and a small spot illustration (overlapping speech bubbles) top-right. Below is a full-width list of hairline-separated rows (~50px). Questions run up to 2 lines, with an ↑ or ↓ arrow at the far right. The open answer is capped at ~420px width.
references.type: Heading in a book serif at ~26px regular. Questions ~13px medium in color. Answers ~10px regular dark grey with ~1.6 line-height.
references.color: Warm off-white ~#FBF8F3 ground, deep violet ~#3B2A6B heading, medium violet ~#7A5AC8 questions and arrows, hairlines ~#E3DDE8, a multicolor spot illustration (pink, green, yellow).
details: Questions are tinted in the brand color, so the list itself carries the color
A scoped heading ('FAQs about Tines professional services'), not just 'FAQ'
One small hand-drawn illustration personalizes an otherwise austere list
Thin arrows instead of chevrons or plus signs
references.why_it_works: Quietly crafted: serif plus a warm ground plus brand-tinted questions feels considered with almost no decoration.
references.trade_adaptation: 'FAQs about our drain cleaning service' (scoped per service page), with questions in the brand color and a small spot drawing of a wrench or pipe.

references.layout: A rounded panel (~12px radius) on a dark page. The left half holds a single-line heading at top-left and nothing else (generous negative space). The right half holds stacked question cards (~6px radius, ~6px gaps); the open card shows the answer and a '×', and closed cards show '+'.
references.type: Heading in a transitional serif at ~20px, with the first word in italic ('*Answers* to your questions'). Questions ~10px medium grotesk. Answers ~9px regular.
references.color: Page ~#111111, panel ~#1C1C1C, question cards ~#262626, white questions, grey ~#9A9A9A answers.
details: Mixing italic and roman serif in one heading is an easy premium move
The empty left half is deliberate: the heading floats like a magazine pull
Small tonal steps (page → panel → card) create depth without borders
references.why_it_works: Restrained luxury. Good for a high-end trade brand (custom remodeler, solar, smart-home electrician) that wants a dark theme.
references.trade_adaptation: Custom remodeler: '*Answers* to your questions', with cards 'How long does a kitchen remodel take?', 'Do you handle permits?', 'Can we live at home during the work?'.

references.layout: A tiny 'FAQ' eyebrow and a 1-line heading at top-left. Below are full-width white rows (~4px radius, ~4px gaps) where the question is set very large. A circular icon sits at the far right: a filled orange minus when open, a grey plus when closed. The open answer is a short bulleted list.
references.type: Heading and questions in a high-contrast display serif. Heading ~28px; questions ~22px regular, which is nearly heading size. Answers ~10px grotesk bullets.
references.color: Light grey ~#F0F0EE ground, white rows, near-black ~#141414 serif, orange ~#FF5A1F active icon, grey ~#BDBDBD inactive icons.
details: The questions are the display type, which flips the usual small-question hierarchy
Only the open item gets color (the filled orange minus), so the state is unmistakable
Few questions (3), each given room
references.why_it_works: Editorial confidence: three big questions read like headlines and invite reading. Ideal for a short, curated FAQ on a home page.
references.trade_adaptation: Home-page FAQ with the three questions that matter: 'How much does a new roof cost?', 'Will insurance cover it?', 'How long will it take?', in a big serif with the brand accent on the open state.

references.layout: A 'Common searches' label with grey chip links above. Below is a 3x2 grid of cards (~8px radius, ~12px gaps). Each card has a heading with a circular arrow button at the top-right, a hairline, then 3 question links, each with a faint arrow at the right. The sixth cell is a dark card ('Haven't found what you need? Get in touch — we're happy to help!') with a glossy 3D speech-bubble sticker bleeding off its top-right corner and a white full-width 'Contact us' button.

references.color: White ground, cards ~#F2F2F2, text ~#1E1E1E, chips ~#EDEDED. Dark card ~#1E1E1E with a green ~#7ED957 and orange ~#FF9A1F 3D bubble, white button.
details: The contact card is a peer in the grid, not an afterthought below it
One playful 3D object breaking the card edge gives the grid a focal point
'Common searches' chips surface the top questions before the grid
references.why_it_works: A help-center pattern scaled down to one section: browsable by topic, with a clear human fallback built into the layout.
references.trade_adaptation: Cards: 'Before your appointment', 'Pricing & financing', 'Warranty & guarantees', 'Emergencies', 'Service area', plus a dark 'Need a human? Call (555) 019-2020' card with a brand-color sticker (a phone or truck).

references.layout: Left (~42%): a 2-line heading, a 2-line grey sub and a small blue button. Right (~44%): question rows (~40px), each with a thin '+' at the far right and a hand-drawn wavy line divider underneath instead of a straight hairline.
references.type: Heading in a neo-grotesk at ~30px regular, white. Sub ~10px grey. Questions ~12px regular white.
references.color: Near-black ~#161616 ground, white text, grey ~#8A8A8A sub, wavy dividers ~#4A4A4A, blue ~#2F7BEA button.
details: Wavy, sketch-like dividers are a single custom detail that makes a standard accordion feel bespoke
Very little else on the page: the detail carries the identity
references.why_it_works: Proof that one custom divider can make a common pattern feel designed rather than generated.
references.trade_adaptation: The divider becomes a trade motif: a wavy water line for a plumber or pool service, a dashed wire for an electrician, a hedge squiggle for a landscaper.

references.layout: A full-width light band. A small quirky character illustration is centered above a centered heading, then a narrow (~380px) centered list of hairline-separated questions with chevrons. The open item gets a colored rule beneath its question, and the answer is indented slightly.
references.type: Heading in a condensed, high-contrast serif at ~30px regular. Questions ~10px regular. Answers ~10px with ~1.6 line-height.
references.color: Light grey ~#F2F2F2 band, ink ~#1A1A1A text, hairlines ~#CFCFCF, dark green ~#2E5A4A rule under the open question, an illustration in yellow ~#F2C230 and navy.
details: The condensed serif heading feels bookish and distinct from the grotesk body
The open state is marked by a colored rule, not a background change
A single mascot-like illustration above the heading adds personality
references.why_it_works: A simple centered accordion made memorable by type choice and one illustration, with minimal effort and real character.
references.trade_adaptation: Family-run handyman or cleaner: a small illustrated mascot (a toolbox or mop character) above 'Frequently asked questions' in a condensed serif, with the open item underlined in the brand color.

references.layout: A centered heading over a narrow (~380px) column. Group labels ('General', 'Pricing & Payment', 'Sessions') sit above clusters of full-width question bars (~4px radius, ~6px gaps) with chevrons. The open bar expands to show answer paragraphs. A sticky bottom bar carries a price summary and a CTA.
references.type: Heading ~16px bold, centered. Group labels ~9px semibold grey. Questions ~9px bold white. Answers ~9px regular.
references.color: Black ~#000000 ground, bars ~#1E1F22, white text, grey ~#9A9A9A labels, brand red ~#E1344B CTA.
details: Group labels split money questions from logistics
A sticky bottom bar ('Starting at $15/month… Sign Up') keeps the conversion path visible throughout
references.why_it_works: Not visually remarkable, but the grouping plus a persistent price-and-CTA bar is a useful conversion mechanic for long FAQs.
references.trade_adaptation: A sticky bar under the FAQ on mobile: 'Same-day service · Flat-rate pricing · Call (555) 017-3300', with groups 'Pricing', 'Scheduling' and 'Warranty'.

takeaways: Always pair the FAQ with a human fallback in the same layout: a sticky left-column contact button, a dark 'Still stuck? Call us' card in the grid, a right-side 'Email us' zone or a sticky bottom bar.
Group questions by the homeowner's worries (Pricing, Scheduling, Warranty, Emergencies). For long lists use two levels: categories with counts, then questions.
Make the open state unmistakable with a single accent (a filled orange minus, a colored rule, a raised white card) and keep closed rows quiet.
Treat answers as sales copy: bullets with bold lead-ins, concrete numbers and a closing benefit sentence. A home-page FAQ can show just 3-5 big questions and link to the full page.
One custom detail is enough to escape the template look: wavy dividers, numbered folder tabs, brand-tinted questions, an italic word in a serif heading, or a spot illustration.
Scope the heading ('FAQs about drain cleaning') on service pages, which also helps local SEO.
A split layout (heading and contact left, accordion right) uses wide screens better than a narrow centered column and keeps the CTA visible.
avoid: A centered 'Frequently Asked Questions' bold heading over a narrow stack of identical grey rounded pills with chevrons (Lattice, Shuttle, Loom, Amie): the default AI-template FAQ.
Dark purple cards with white plus-in-circle icons (Mixpanel): SaaS pricing-page boilerplate.
Two-column boxed accordions with blue chevrons and bold small questions (HubSpot): dated corporate look.
Giant pastel pill rows with tiny arrow icons and huge padding (Loom): low density and low trust.
An FAQ with no contact route, or a contact CTA pushed into a separate section far below.
Non-collapsible walls of Q&A text with inline pink links (Wellfound).
Generic questions that are really ads ('Why should I choose X?'). Answer real objections: cost, timing, mess, insurance, warranty.
